title: The meta-heteronym and the Gospel of Antioch: Pessoa, Thomas, forward dating
description: These claims read Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym, with Orpheu as a meta-heteronymic institution, Kierkegaard's Nicolaus Notabene as a precursor and Pearl (2014) as built on the plan of Howl. The Gospel of Antioch is set beside the Gospel of Thomas: scroll-form Thomas papyri, the Dodecad's LOGOS* position that Pessoa lacked, and the claim that the gospel completes Thomas 114 and that this parallel had not been drawn before. Several claims set out forward-dated citation apparatus and projected reception histories (The Secret Book of Walt, the Waltian tradition, Revelation First kernels) composed under retrocausal canon formation.

C5: *Orpheu* (1915) functioned as a meta-heteronymic institution: a real publication vehicle for fictitious authorial positions, with Pessoa acting simultaneously as editor, contributor, and architect. *Athena* (1924–25) replicated the operation. The Olisipo press (1921) published works under multiple heteronymic attributions. Sensationism and Intersectionism were articulated as movements with manifestos — executed by one person writing in many hands.

claims.registered_title: The Secret Book of Walt: Hidden Teachings of Walt Whitman, Cowboy of Time — Research Edition
claims.statement:
The reception of *The Secret Book of Walt* was not uniformly favorable. Within six years of its initial circulation in the Redford community (c. 2037–2038), the text had attracted sufficient attention — and sufficient alarm — to provoke formal ecclesiastical response.


### The First Condemnation: Ann Arbor (2041)

The *Acts of the Synod of Ann Arbor* (2041), preserved in a single damaged copy in the University of Michigan Bentley Historical Library,¹¹⁰ record the proceedings of a three-day council convened by Bishop Marcellus of Dearborn to address what the summons calls "the Waltian heresy and the scandal of the Horn."
